_comment: urlscan.io endpoint path templates + paging/budget knobs for wp_net.urlscan_hostname (the Pro `hostname` lifecycle index — every A/AAAA/NS/MX/SOA record, CT first-seen, zonefile first-seen and scan sighting urlscan ever recorded for one host, as DAILY rows). Measured live 2026-09-03 on a Pro team key + OpenAPI (docs.urlscan.io/apis/urlscan-openapi/hostnames/gethostnamehistory): GET /api/v1/hostname/{host} takes `limit` (10..10000, default 1000) and `pageState` (cursor), NO source/type filter; returns `results` rows {seen_on (YYYY-MM-DD), source ∈ ct|scan|pdns|zonefile|scan-link|scan-cert-subject, sub_id 'TYPE#rdata' (may be empty), first_seen, last_seen, data_type ('json'|null), data}. Rows are PER DAY per record (568 of the first 1000 example.com rows were recent daily A/NS rows), newest first, so the client MUST fold rows by sub_id into eras and MUST mark eras that touch the oldest day reached as left-censored when the walk is truncated — otherwise a busy host's hosting 'start' is a pagination artefact. Per-source summary rows carry seen_on 2100-01-01/2200-01-01 and null data. Overrides the inline _USCAN_FALLBACK in wp_net.py; a missing/bad file degrades to that fallback with a warning. HOSTNAME-ONLY by design — the livescan/scan submission surface is out of scope for the collector (outbound, actionguard-gated).

endpoints._comment: paths joined to https://urlscan.io; {host} is the bare hostname; {limit} the page size; {page_state} the opaque cursor from the previous page.
endpoints._quotas_comment: ENTITLEMENT probe (free, account-side, no target touched). Measured live 2026-09-04 on a Pro team key: body {scope, limits}; limits.products = ['livescan','pro'] (the tier signal: 'pro' present -> tier pro, present-but-without-pro -> free, field ABSENT -> unknown, never free); limits.features = [...]; per-scope limits.<search|retrieve|public|unlisted|private>.day.{limit,used,remaining,percent,reset}; limits.maxSearchResults. /user/username also carries isPro but with account-holder name/e-mail — never persisted, never read by the probe.

hostname._comment: page_limit = rows per page (API max 10000 — one retrieve credit per page regardless of size, so the max is the cheapest way to reach a drop-catch host's years-old parking era); max_pages bounds the walk and sets `truncated`; era_types are the pdns sub_id prefixes turned into dated eras; summary_seen_on marks the per-source rollup rows read for the *_first fields and never treated as daily observations.

verdict._comment: Result `labels` that describe page STRUCTURE / hosting class, not a finding (measured on a benign example.com result: domain.apexdomain, content.rootdir, hosting.cdn). A verdict row for the evidence ledger is emitted only on SIGNAL — malicious (overall or engines), overall score > 0, a brand match, or a label outside this set — so a benign estate host never fills Appendix B with non-evidence. Add a label here when it shows up on benign scans; never remove a `visual.*`/`threat.*`-class label.

dom_assets._comment: Bounds for wp_net.urlscan_dom_assets: when a page is recovered from a urlscan DOM capture (the live site is unreachable), fetch that SAME scan's own stored JS/CSS responses (data.requests[].response.hash -> /responses/<sha256>/) so the asset layer (extract_api_endpoints / extract_app_downloads) still has bundle text to read instead of the empty result a failed same-origin fetch would otherwise leave. max_resources bounds the /responses/ fetch count (each is a licensed call under an API key); extensions/mime_prefixes select which of the scan's requests are worth fetching.

gated._comment: A urlscan scan that captured a GATE instead of the site — Chrome error page, anti-bot fake error, a blocking HTTP status or a challenge interstitial (Cloudflare 'Just a moment...', 'Attention Required!', DDoS-Guard …). Its DOM/assets are the CDN's challenge kit, never the operator's, so wp_net.urlscan_gated_reason flags it and urlscan_dom / urlscan_dom_all skip it in favour of the newest UNGATED scan. Ported from Quarry urlscan_target_signals.gated_reason. `labels` maps a result label to the reason string; `statuses` are page.status codes that mean the crawler was blocked/errored; `titles` are whitespace-collapsed, lower-cased page titles matched EXACTLY (a substring match would flag a real page titled 'Access denied — login').

resubmit._comment: When every stored scan of a target is gated, the consented --submit path scans ONCE from the target's ccTLD country (urlscan `country`) with the Android UA (`customagent`) — a geo/UA-fenced kit often gates foreign desktop crawlers only. generic_cctlds are ccTLDs sold as generic TLDs whose country says nothing about the audience (no country is sent for them); cctld_aliases maps a ccTLD to its ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code where they differ. Ported from Quarry urlscan_target_signals.cctld_country.

field_search._comment: Pro content-index FIELDS the cross-type auto-pivot loop may query via wp_recon.urlscan_field_query. `fields` maps a pivot_map route short-name (or the corpus field itself) to the Lucene field key urlscan accepts. page.title / filename / files.filename / hash are free-or-Pro; text.content, content.identifiers.*, links.domains, frames.domains, websockets.domains, dom.hash, text.hash need Pro. TRON wallets are NOT an identifier type — they go through text.content. Edit here when urlscan adds a field; never hardcode field names in the proposer.

host_rung_class._comment: Default rung_class applied to HOST hits from a non-identifier field search. string/filename/title/hash are kit (collecting ≠ attributing). Identifier searches override via identifier_rungs.
host_rung_class.page.title: title

identifier_rungs._comment: content.identifiers:{type} → rung_class. google.* analytics IDs, telegram bot-tokens and discord webhooks are OWNER (may edge). wallet.* is wallet.operator unless the address is labelled exchange in exchange_wallets.json (neighbour). telegram.username / html-id / generic API tokens are kit. Unknown identifier types fall through to token.other (kit). TRON is absent on purpose — route through text.content.
